takeaway: Venous ulcers sit in the gaiter area and are treated with elevation and four-layer bandaging; exclude coexisting ischaemia first. The correct statement is that elevation aids treatment.

question.text: A 74-year-old man has a long history of bilateral leg ulceration. Which of the following statements regarding venous ulcers is correct?

lines.text: Venous ulcers are typically found in the gaiter area, around the ankle.
They have a sloping edge, a sloughy base and a moderate amount of exudate.
The surrounding skin can be hyperpigmented, with lipodermatosclerosis.
Treatment is by elevation, so the correct statement is that elevation aids in treatment.
The other part is four-layer bandaging, with regular dressings.
But always exclude coexisting ischaemia first, and treat it if present, because compression can compromise the blood supply further.
lines.say: But always exclude coexisting ischaemia first, and treat it if present, because compression can compromise the blood supply further. (sigh)
